# Known issue #413: VideoGrabber (Windows): setup() returns true while the media type is not RGB32 and every frame is black (v0.7 part of #276)

## Summary
v0.7 part carved out of #276. On Windows, `VideoGrabber::setup()` can return true while every frame is dropped, because the current media type is still YUY2 / NV12 / MJPG, not RGB32. title: Known issue #408: Serial (Windows): the port is opened without FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, so available() and reads wait behind a WriteFile in progress
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #408, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #408: Serial (Windows): the port is opened without FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, so available() and reads wait behind a WriteFile in progress

## Summary
On Windows, `Serial` opens the port without `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`. The OS then serializes every call on the handle. While one thread is inside `WriteFile`, another thread's `available()` (`ClearCommError`) and reads wait for that write. When a worker writes back to back, the writer can go first again, so the wait is not bounded to one write.

#379 fixes the TrussC-side starvation with a shared lock. The OS-level wait on Windows remains, and this issue covers it.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #400: OscReceiver: setup() always shares the port, so a second instance binds without error and unicast OSC reaches only one of them
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #400, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #400: OscReceiver: setup() always shares the port, so a second instance binds without error and unicast OSC reaches only one of them

## Summary
`OscReceiver::setup(port)` always turns on `SO_REUSEADDR` and `SO_REUSEPORT` before it binds. This is on purpose: several apps can then share one multicast port. The side effect hits plain unicast use. If a second copy of the app starts, or another receiver on the same PC already holds the port, `setup()` still returns `true`. Nothing is logged. Unicast datagrams then reach only one of the sockets, so one instance gets no messages (or only some of them), and neither side sees an error.

This needs a decision on the default, so it is filed with options.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #387: Linux VideoPlayer: the NV12 hardware-decode draw ignores the matrix, color and Fbo size, and resets sokol_gl's matrices
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #387, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #387: Linux VideoPlayer: the NV12 hardware-decode draw ignores the matrix, color and Fbo size, and resets sokol_gl's matrices

## Summary
On Linux, when hardware decoding is active and frames come out as NV12 (CUDA / VAAPI), `VideoPlayer::draw()` goes through a dedicated NV12 shader. That path ignores the current matrix, `setColor()` and the render target size. Afterwards it also overwrites sokol_gl's projection and modelview. Software decoding and the other platforms draw through `texture_.draw()`, so the same app draws the video differently depending on whether the machine has a hardware decoder.

This is the same pattern as HAP-Q in #283, and gets the same fix.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #383: Headless: a Ctrl+C just before the loop's flag reset is lost, and Ctrl+C / requestExit() is not read during a long catch-up pass
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #383, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #383: Headless: a Ctrl+C just before the loop's flag reset is lost, and Ctrl+C / requestExit() is not read during a long catch-up pass

## Summary
`runHeadlessApp()` has two small gaps in how it stops.

1. It installs the SIGINT / SIGTERM / console handlers first and resets `headless::running = true` afterwards. A Ctrl+C that lands between the two is overwritten and lost.
2. The fixed-step catch-up loop does not read `headless::running` or `app.isExitRequested()`. After a stall, Ctrl+C, SIGTERM or `App::requestExit()` only takes effect once every due step has run. On main every headless app is affected, because main has no step cap. With #313 only `setMaxUpdateSteps(<= 0)` is affected.

On POSIX, repeated Ctrl+C does not help. On Windows, the second Ctrl+C (#368) ends the process without `exit()` / `cleanup()`.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #382: tc::Thread: a subclass that waits still terminates when destroyed on its own worker (waitForThread() joins itself)
text:

# Known issue #382: tc::Thread: a subclass that waits still terminates when destroyed on its own worker (waitForThread() joins itself)

## Summary
A `Thread` subclass that follows the documented rule and calls `waitForThread()` in its own destructor still calls `std::terminate` when it is destroyed on its own worker thread. That happens when `threadedFunction()` does `delete this` or drops the last `shared_ptr`, or when a `thread_local` owner is released at thread exit. `waitForThread()` joins its own thread. `~Thread()` already detects this case and detaches, and ofThread's `waitForThread()` returns early here. `waitForThread()` should do the same.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #380: Windows: log and error text in the loaders and setLogFile still uses the strict pathToUtf8, so a name with an unpaired surrogate throws
text:

# Known issue #380: Windows: log and error text in the loaders and setLogFile still uses the strict pathToUtf8, so a name with an unpaired surrogate throws

## Summary
On Windows, `pathToUtf8()` throws `std::system_error` for a name that is not valid UTF-16, which NTFS allows (an unpaired surrogate). #368 made it public and kept it strict on purpose: it is for strings that go back into a path. For text people read, #368 added `internal::pathToDisplayUtf8()`, which writes U+FFFD instead of throwing. It also added `LogStream << fs::path`, which uses it.

Several loaders, and `Logger::setLogFile()`, still build their log lines and `LoadResult` messages with the strict `pathToUtf8()`. For such a name they throw instead of loading or returning a failure. The worst cases are files the OS opens fine through the wide API. The WAV / MP3 / FLAC / OGG buffers, `SoundStream` and `setLogFile()` all throw because of their log text alone. So does Windows AAC, if Media Foundation opens the file. `setLogFile()` throws after the file is open and leaves the Logger half-updated.

#368 listed these sites as a follow-up. None of them is a regression from #368.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

text:

# Known issue #377: Windows hot reload: the .def generator drops every TrussC symbol at a .lib offset below 0x100000 (guest link fails with LNK2019)

## Summary
On Windows, a hot reload host exports TrussC through a generated `trussc_exports.def`. The script parses `dumpbin /LINKERMEMBER:1` with a regex that needs at least 6 hex digits before the symbol name. dumpbin does not zero-pad the member offset. So every public symbol of an object in the first 1 MB of TrussC.lib (offset < 0x100000) is left out of the .def. The host then does not export those symbols, and a guest that calls one of them fails to link with LNK2019. Which functions are affected depends on the order and size of the objects in the lib, so it changes with the generator and the build config.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #375: Build: app and addon source/shader globs lack CONFIGURE_DEPENDS, so an existing app tree misses a new src/*.cpp or src/*.glsl

## Summary
`trussc_app()` collects an app's sources and shaders with plain `file(GLOB_RECURSE ...)`. These globs run only at configure time. An app's existing build tree does not see a `.cpp` or `.glsl` added to `src/` later, and `trusscli build` does not reconfigure in that case. So the new file is not compiled, and the build fails with a link error or a missing `*.glsl.h`. Addons have the same gap, both in the auto-collect globs in `use_addon.cmake` and in the `src/` globs of most in-repo addons' own `CMakeLists.txt`. PR #314 fixes this for core's own globs with `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS` (#366). This issue is the app and addon follow-up.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #373: trusscli: on Windows, update and addon add/remove write addons.make and CMakeLists.txt with CRLF, so build_all.py leaves the tree -dirty

## Summary
On Windows, `trusscli` writes `addons.make` and `CMakeLists.txt` through a text-mode `ofstream`, so each line ends in CRLF. The repo commits both files with LF (`* text=auto eol=lf`). `examples/build_all.py` runs `trusscli update` on every project it builds. On Windows that marks these files modified even though their content has not changed, and `git describe --dirty` then reports `-dirty`. The fix is to open these three writers in binary mode. The rest of the codebase already does this when text must be written byte for byte.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #364: Serial: RX bytes lost during a main-thread stall are dropped silently on desktop; Windows discards the ClearCommError overrun flags

## Summary
On desktop, `Serial` has no receive buffer of its own. Incoming bytes wait in the OS driver queue until the app polls on the main thread. If the app stalls longer than that queue can hold, bytes are lost, and TrussC reports nothing on any desktop platform.

On Windows the driver does report the loss, but TrussC throws the report away: `Serial::available()` calls `ClearCommError()`, which returns and clears the error flags (receive overrun, queue overflow, framing, parity), and only the queue length is used. The lost bytes then look like a protocol bug in the app.

The Android backend already avoids the stall loss: a worker thread drains the port into a capped 1 MiB buffer and warns when it drops data.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #362: Shader: setTexture()/setUniform() slots are not range-checked; texture slots 12+ write past samplers[] in a stack sg_bindings
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #362, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #362: Shader: setTexture()/setUniform() slots are not range-checked; texture slots 12+ write past samplers[] in a stack sg_bindings

## Summary
`Shader::setTexture()` and `Shader::setUniform()` accept any `int` slot. The texture slot is later used as the index into both `views[32]` and `samplers[12]` of a local `sg_bindings` (sokol's per-draw binding struct). The uniform slot is passed to `sg_apply_uniforms()`, which supports slots 0-7. TrussC checks neither range. sokol's only checks are asserts and debug validation, and for textures only an end-of-struct canary. Both are compiled out when `NDEBUG` is set, which includes the default RelWithDebInfo build.

The real limits are different for the two arrays. Texture (view) slots 12-31 are valid in sokol, but for them the `samplers[slot]` write overflows. A texture slot of 12-31 writes the sampler past `samplers[]`: slot 12 overwrites `_end_canary`, and slots 13-31 write past the end of the struct on the stack. A slot of 32 or more, or a negative one, corrupts other fields of the struct or the stack. A uniform slot outside 0-7 makes the backend index its per-shader tables out of range.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #361: macOS: captureWindowAsync can overwrite a staging texture before a recorder frame has read it
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #361, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #361: macOS: captureWindowAsync can overwrite a staging texture before a recorder frame has read it

## Summary
On macOS, `internal::captureWindowAsync()` copies each window capture into one of 3 static staging textures, round-robin. A staging texture is a CPU-readable copy of the drawable. The consumer reads it later, in the Metal completion handler. Nothing checks that the previous capture in a slot has been read before the slot is reused. The ring is a single static, shared by all windows.

With one screen `VideoRecorder` and nothing else capturing, the ring is just deep enough. Any other capture on sokol's queue that is issued while 3 recorder captures are pending takes the oldest pending slot. The GPU blit overwrites it before the recorder's handler reads it, so that frame is encoded with later pixels. Nothing is logged.

Affected: `grabScreen()` in `update()`, `grabScreen()` in an `afterFrame` listener registered after the recorder, a second screen recorder, and `saveScreenshot()`/MCP captures of a recorded secondary window. Main-window `saveScreenshot()`/MCP captures are safe, but only because of listener order (details below).

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #360: iOS: device enumeration (tc_get_audio_state, AudioEngine::listDevices) changes, activates and then deactivates the AVAudioSession

## Summary
On iOS, TrussC's two device-enumeration paths change the shared `AVAudioSession`. Each opens a throwaway miniaudio context with the default config. On iOS, miniaudio's context init sets the session category to PlayAndRecord with DefaultToSpeaker and activates the session; its uninit deactivates the session. Apple documents that deactivating a session stops running audio I/O.

- `tc_get_audio_state` (documented as "read-only; never starts the engine") takes this path when the engine has no context (no `Sound` loaded, or after `shutdown()`).
- `AudioEngine::listDevices()` takes it on every call, including while the engine is playing.

macOS, Windows, Linux and Android have no such side effect.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #358: trusscli: build no longer reconfigures after TC_HOT_RELOAD is toggled (the #35 pre-check was lost in a merge)

## Summary
`TC_HOT_RELOAD(...)` turns on hot reload for an app. Hot reload is switched at configure time. So when the macro is added or removed, a pre-build check stops the build once, and the next build reconfigures. PR #35 also gave `trusscli build` a pre-check that reconfigures first, so trusscli works in one step. That pre-check was lost when #35 was merged. Today `trusscli build` (and `trusscli run`) fails once after every toggle, and the second run succeeds, the same as plain CMake. The CMake message and the docs still promise the one-step behaviour.

This is a regression from a merge conflict, not a missing feature.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #354: Windows batch scripts: `if errorlevel 1` misses negative exit codes (build_win.bat since #297, generated build-web.bat)

# Known issue #354: Windows batch scripts: `if errorlevel 1` misses negative exit codes (build_win.bat since #297, generated build-web.bat)

## Summary
#297 changed the configure check in `tools/build_win.bat` from `if %ERRORLEVEL% neq 0 (` to `if errorlevel 1 (`, and used the same form for the new retry check. `if errorlevel 1` is true only for exit codes of 1 or more. When a Windows process ends on an NTSTATUS code (a crash, or a DLL that fails to load), cmd stores a negative ERRORLEVEL. Both configure checks now let that through. The script then skips the retry and the "CMake configuration failed" message and goes on to `cmake --build`. The old `neq 0` form caught these codes. The PR description does not mention the switch.

The `build-web.bat` that trusscli writes into Windows projects has the same pattern after both of its `cmake` calls. That one predates #297.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #345: tcxImGui: touched record misses ColorEdit drops, records unchanged combos, keeps stale combo item
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #345, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #345: tcxImGui: touched record misses ColorEdit drops, records unchanged combos, keeps stale combo item

## Summary
tcxImGui keeps a "touched" record: the widgets the user changed by hand, which an AI reads over MCP with `tcx_imgui_get_touched`. A per-widget "value hook" (`IMGUI_TC_ITEM_VALUE`, a TrussC patch to imgui) runs when a value widget returns and decides whether it was edited. It has three gaps for Combo and ColorEdit:

1. A colour dropped onto a `ColorEdit` by drag-and-drop changes the variable, but it is not recorded unless the widget was already in the record.
2. Typing in a filter field inside a combo popup, or clicking the item that is already selected, records the combo, although its value did not change.
3. In the frame where the user picks a new combo item, the entry pairs the new index with the old item text, e.g. `{value: 2, item: "Low"}`. The frame entry corrects itself the next time the combo is drawn. The touched record keeps the mismatch if the pick hides the combo.

Cases 1 and 2 have one cause: the hook decides "edited" from ImGui's Edited status flag and its own edit counter, not from the value. For a plain `Combo()` there is a second path: the combo-popup branch of the ItemInfo hook creates the combo's entry on any Selectable press, before `Combo()` has decided whether the index changed. Case 3 copies the preview text without checking that it matches the index.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #340: tcxImGui: imgui buffers are fixed at 65,536 vertices; past that, top windows and popups are not drawn

## Summary
`ImGuiManager::setup()` creates each window's sokol_imgui context without setting `max_vertices`, so it gets the default of 65,536 vertices (and 3 × 65,536 indices). The buffers are allocated once and never grow, and `imguiSetup()` has no way to raise the limit. When a frame's ImGui output is larger, `simgui_render()` logs an error and stops copying. The draw list that overflows and all later ones are not drawn. ImGui orders draw lists back to front, so the lost ones are the topmost windows, popups, combo lists, tooltips and the foreground list. This repeats every frame.

title: Known issue #337: Linux VideoPlayer: load() decodes the whole audio track into RAM (about 1.4 GB per hour), and an allocation failure leaks the player
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #337, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #337: Linux VideoPlayer: load() decodes the whole audio track into RAM (about 1.4 GB per hour), and an allocation failure leaks the player

## Summary
On Linux, `VideoPlayer::load()` decodes the whole audio track up front. The result is one float stereo buffer at the engine sample rate, kept in memory until `close()`. At 48 kHz that is 384 KB per second, about 1.4 GB per hour. `load()` blocks on the calling thread until the whole file has been read once. The macOS (AVPlayer) and Windows (IMFMediaEngine) backends do not decode audio up front.

This is a known limit, not an oversight. PR #28, which added Linux audio, says: "Pre-decodes audio into `SoundBuffer` at load time for stable A/V sync" and "Pre-loading the full audio buffer works well for videos up to ~10 minutes. A streaming approach for longer content is left as future work." This issue tracks that deferred work (enhancement, needs a decision).

One part is a plain bug: if the allocation fails, `std::bad_alloc` escapes `loadPlatform()` and the whole player implementation leaks.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #335: Touch: events carry at most 8 points (7 on iOS), and the cap can drop the finger that changed, so its begin or end is lost

## Summary
A touch event carries at most 8 points. The cap is applied inside sokol_app_tc (TrussC's fork of sokol_app), in each platform backend, before TrussC sees the event: iOS keeps 7, Android and Web keep 8. The backends keep the first points in the platform's order, not the point that changed. When the changed finger falls past the cap, `touchPressed` / `touchReleased` fire with no point marked `changed`. Apps that track fingers by id then never add or never remove that finger. Nothing is logged.

text:

# Known issue #334: Drag and drop / clipboard: fixed buffers cap drops at 16 files and clipboard text at 64 KB, and X11 rejects INCR pastes, mostly without a log

## Summary
File drops and clipboard text go through fixed buffers in `sokol_app_tc.h`, TrussC's fork of sokol_app (the windowing layer). TrussC sizes these buffers once at startup.

- Drop: `max_dropped_files = 16` is hard-coded, with no setting. A larger drop delivers the first 16 files, and no backend reports the rest. A path of 2048 bytes or more aborts the whole drop on macOS, X11 and Raspberry Pi. On Windows, a long ASCII path arrives truncated; only a path whose UTF-8 form overflows aborts the drop. Only the Raspberry Pi and web backends log the abort.
- Clipboard: `WindowSettings::clipboardSize` (default 65536) sizes the buffer. A larger paste is cut or returned empty. On X11 (desktop and Raspberry Pi), pastes that the source app sends by INCR (X11's chunked transfer for large selections) are always rejected, whatever the buffer size. `setClipboardString()` logs "Text truncated", but that is wrong on every platform: some copy the full text, some copy nothing, and Raspberry Pi copies a byte-cut prefix.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #332: Frame loop: ticks that don't draw never call sg_commit(), so GPU work from update() piles up (EVENT_DRIVEN) or aborts Debug builds (draw rate below tick rate)
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #332, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #332: Frame loop: ticks that don't draw never call sg_commit(), so GPU work from update() piles up (EVENT_DRIVEN) or aborts Debug builds (draw rate below tick rate)

## Summary
`sg_commit()` ends a sokol frame. TrussC's frame loop calls it only in `present()`, and a tick that doesn't draw skips `present()`. With independent update, `update()` also runs on ticks that don't draw. Any GPU work it records there (Fbo passes, texture/buffer uploads) stays in the open sokol frame until the next drawn tick.

This hits two documented setups:

- **Draw rate below the tick rate**, e.g. `setIndependentFps(60, 30)`. About every other tick doesn't draw, so two ticks share one sokol frame. A texture uploaded in every `update()` passes TrussC's once-per-frame guard (keyed on `sapp_frame_count()`, which advances every tick) and hits sokol's `VALIDATE_UPDIMG_ONCE`. That is a panic, so a Debug build aborts within the first few ticks.
- **EVENT_DRIVEN draw**, e.g. `setIndependentFps(60, EVENT_DRIVEN)`, which the docs recommend for GUI/tool apps. The frame stays open until the next `redraw()`. Per-frame buffers rewind only when a frame ends, so they keep growing while the app is idle. On WebGPU the uniform staging buffer overflows instead of growing.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

text:

# Known issue #331: Matrix stack: past 63 nested pushMatrix / Node levels, every later 2D draw of the frame is dropped

## Summary
`RenderContext::pushMatrix()` pushes two stacks: TrussC's own, which grows, and sokol_gl's, which has a fixed 64 entries. sokol_gl is the immediate-mode layer that records TrussC's 2D shapes, text and images. On the 64th nested push, sokol_gl sets its context error flag. While that flag is set, `sgl_end()` records nothing. So every sokol_gl draw after the overflow is dropped until the end of the frame, not just drawn with the wrong transform. The warning in `present()` says that transforms are wrong. An overflow inside an Fbo pass is never reported.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #330: build_win.bat: a VS 2022 build cache is kept after VS 2026 is installed alongside, and the build fails
text:

# Known issue #330: build_win.bat: a VS 2022 build cache is kept after VS 2026 is installed alongside, and the build fails

## Summary
`tools/build_win.bat` builds trusscli, the TrussC project generator and command-line tool, into `tools/build`. Before configuring, it runs a stale-cache guard: a check that deletes `CMakeCache.txt` when the cache can no longer work. The guard only checks whether the cached compiler file still exists. The configure retry added in #297 only runs when configure fails.

When VS 2026 is installed next to VS 2022, neither of them fires. VS 2022 stays installed unless the user removes it. The VS 2022 `cl.exe` recorded in the cache still exists, so the cache is kept, and configure succeeds. But `vcvarsall` has loaded the VS 2026 environment. The mismatch first shows up in `cmake --build`, which has no retry and says nothing about the cache. Every later run that recompiles something fails the same way until the user deletes `tools/build` by hand.

#251 says the guard exists for "local users who upgrade Visual Studio". Installing side by side is a normal way to upgrade. The gap predates #297; that PR did not cause it.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #328: Coverage generator: class-level TC_PLATFORMS guards only the constructor; [[deprecated]] on ctors/classes ignored
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #328, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #328: Coverage generator: class-level TC_PLATFORMS guards only the constructor; [[deprecated]] on ctors/classes ignored

## Summary
`docs/reference/emit-coverage.js` (added in #250) generates `coverage_generated.cpp`. That file makes the AllFeaturesExample CI canary reference every documented API on every platform. The generator takes each reference's `#if` guard and its deprecation filter only from that symbol's own entry in `reference-data.json`. Annotations written on a class or on a single constructor never reach the generated code:

1. **A class-level `TC_PLATFORMS` guards only the class's constructor.** Every method and field of the class is referenced on all six platforms. Ten classes have a class-level list today: `Window`, `TcpServer`, `TcpClient`, `UdpSocket`, `Serial`, `Thread`, `VideoPlayer`, `VideoGrabber`, `VideoWriter` and `ScreenRecorder`. Function-level and method-level `TC_PLATFORMS` already become guards, so class-level lists are the odd one out.
2. **`[[deprecated]]` or `TC_PLATFORMS` on a single constructor is lost.** `structure.js` stores a constructor as `{ params, args }` and nothing else.
3. **`[[deprecated]]` on a whole class skips only its constructors.** Every method and field is still referenced through `af::val<Owner>()`.

`TC_PLATFORMS("...")` is the attribute macro that lists the platforms an API works on. Nothing fails today. Items 2 and 3 break the per-PR lane on the next constructor or class deprecation. Item 1 is an inconsistency with the generator's own documented contract.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #327: Fbo: an unbalanced push/pop inside an Fbo pass misplaces later nodes and stops 2D drawing in other Fbos
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #327, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #327: Fbo: an unbalanced push/pop inside an Fbo pass misplaces later nodes and stops 2D drawing in other Fbos

## Summary
#232 (fixed in #247) contains an unbalanced `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()` in two places. Per node, `Node::drawTree()` puts the depth back with `restoreStackDepth()`. Per frame, `present()` resets the stacks. Both assume one sokol_gl context.

sokol_gl is the immediate-mode layer TrussC draws its 2D shapes, text and images with. Each sokol_gl context keeps its own matrix stack, 64 entries deep. An Fbo pass switches to a separate context, shared by all Fbos with the same format and sample count. So an imbalance between `fbo.begin()` and `fbo.end()` breaks in two ways:

1. **Inside a node's `draw()`:** the node fix-up runs after `fbo.end()` has switched back to the screen context. Its sokol_gl pops land on a context that never saw the matching push. For the rest of the frame, the node's children lose the node's transform and later nodes lose an ancestor transform. The log shows a misleading "underflow (sgl_pop_matrix without a push)". Before #247 the screen context stayed paired in this case, so #247 made this sub-case worse.
2. **Fbo contexts are never reset or checked:** the frame-end reset and the stack-error report cover only the screen context. A push left open in an Fbo pass raises the shared Fbo context's depth by one per pass. Once it reaches the top, the next push on that context overflows, and every later 2D draw in every Fbo that shares the context is dropped for the rest of the frame, every frame. Nothing is logged.

Both have one cause: nothing checks the stack …

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #324: MCP: a tool reply with invalid UTF-8 fails the whole call (tcx_imgui_get_widgets, tc_get_audio_state)
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #324, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #324: MCP: a tool reply with invalid UTF-8 fails the whole call (tcx_imgui_get_widgets, tc_get_audio_state)

## Summary
TrussC's built-in MCP server (the JSON-RPC endpoint that lets an AI agent inspect and drive a running app) serializes every tool reply with nlohmann's default `dump()`. That mode throws on any string that is not valid UTF-8. The throw is caught, and the whole call becomes a JSON-RPC error. So one bad string anywhere in a reply hides the rest of it.

Two tools on main can return such strings today:
- `tcx_imgui_get_widgets` / `tcx_imgui_get_touched` (tcxImGui addon): `captureValue()` cuts text fields at 64 KiB without looking at UTF-8, so the cut can split a multi-byte character.
- `tc_get_audio_state`: on POSIX a playing voice's file path is passed through as raw filename bytes.

The codebase already fixed the same crash once, in tcxCurl, by passing `error_handler_t::replace` to `dump()`. The MCP server should do the same.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #323: tcxImGui: ImGuiManager destructor touches already-destroyed widget registries after std::exit()
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #323, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #323: tcxImGui: ImGuiManager destructor touches already-destroyed widget registries after std::exit()

## Summary
#244 added `forgetContext(imguiCtx_)` to `ImGuiManager::shutdown()`. `forgetContext` clears two static registries that the ImGui MCP tools read. `detail::contexts()` holds per-context state, including the owner tag that every context gets. `detail::touched()` lists widgets the user changed by hand.

`shutdown()` also runs from `~ImGuiManager` during static destruction. The code uses `sg_isvalid()` to tell that path apart from the live one. The check fails when an app ends with `std::exit()` (or `::exit()`) from inside a frame or event handler:
- Sokol's cleanup callback never runs, so `sg_isvalid()` is still true.
- `forgetContext` then runs on `detail::contexts()` and `detail::touched()`.
- Those function-local statics were constructed after the manager registry, so they are destroyed before it.

The result is undefined behaviour at exit in every tcxImGui app that ends through `std::exit()`, with or without MCP. It is likely a crash with libc++ (macOS) and MSVC (Windows).

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #320: Multi-window: setSize() right after createWindow() uses DPI scale 1.0 until the window's first tick

## Summary
Since #237, `subApp->setSize()` resizes the sub-App's own window from any context. That includes the main App's `setup()` or a key handler, right after `createWindow()` + `setApp()`. If the call comes before the new window's first tick (its first per-window frame callback), it converts sizes with a DPI scale of 1.0 instead of the window's real scale. On a HiDPI display the window then comes out the wrong size. It is 2x too large on a Retina Mac in pixel-perfect mode, and 1/scale too small on Windows/X11 in the default logical mode. The same call one frame later is correct. The cause: `createWindow()` never sets `WindowContext::dpiScale`, and only the tick writes it.

title: Known issue #319: Windows: setWindowSize() and the main App's setSize() ignore display scaling, so the window comes out too small
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #319, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #319: Windows: setWindowSize() and the main App's setSize() ignore display scaling, so the window comes out too small

## Summary
On Windows, `setWindowSizeLogical()` passes its logical width and height straight to `AdjustWindowRectEx` / `SetWindowPos`. The process is per-monitor-v2 DPI aware, so those calls take physical pixels. On a display that is not at 100% scaling, the main window therefore comes out 1/scale of the requested size. At 150%, `setWindowSize(800, 600)` gives a window of 533x400 logical.

Two callers reach this function: the global `setWindowSize()` on the main window, and the main-App branch of `App::setSize()`. Secondary windows go through `Window::setSize()`, which does scale. So since #237, `mainApp->setSize(800, 600)` and `subApp->setSize(800, 600)` give windows that differ by the DPI factor. The defect itself is older than #237.

`Window::setSize()` has two smaller problems of the same kind: it scales by sokol's `dpi_scale` (1.0 for a `highDpi = false` window) instead of the window DPI, and it computes the frame with system-DPI metrics.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #318: Window::setApp(): swapping or removing a window's App skips the outgoing App's exit() and cleanup()

## Summary

Since #224 added `App::getWindow()`, `getWindow()->setApp(...)` makes per-window scene switching a one-liner, so more code will take this path. Whether a swap should tear the App down or only detach it is an owner decision, because the codebase has precedents both ways.

title: Known issue #317: GPU pools: closing a window leaks sgl pipelines; sgl context pool (4) and sg shader pool (32) left at sokol defaults
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #317, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #317: GPU pools: closing a window leaks sgl pipelines; sgl context pool (4) and sg shader pool (32) left at sokol defaults

## Summary
Three problems with sokol's fixed-size resource pools. sokol_gl (sgl) is the immediate-mode layer TrussC draws shapes with. Each sgl pipeline is built from 5 sokol_gfx (sg) pipelines.

1. `Window::close()` destroys the secondary window's sgl context but not the sgl pipelines built for it. Each open/close cycle leaks 2-4 sgl pipelines, which hold 10-20 of the 256 sg pipeline slots. After roughly 10-20 cycles the sg pipeline pool is full for the whole app.
2. `sgl_desc_t.context_pool_size` is never set. The sokol default is 4 contexts, including the default one. Each secondary window and each distinct Fbo `(sampleCount, format)` takes one. After that, the next one gets an invalid context. That Fbo draws no 2D for the rest of the run, or the window shows only its clear color.
3. `sg_desc.shader_pool_size` is never set (sokol default: 32). Each loaded `Shader` takes one slot. TrussC's internal shaders are created lazily and never checked. Once the pool is full, PBR, point, shadow, IBL and Fbo-mip drawing gets an invalid shader.

In all three cases TrussC caches the invalid handle and keeps using it.
- Cases 1 and 3: Debug builds abort in sokol validation. Release builds skip the affected draws, and case 1 can dereference NULL.
- Case 2 is silent in Debug and Release alike. Every sgl call on the invalid context returns early.

The only trace is a sokol line on stderr, which bypasses tc::Logger today (#265).

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

## Summary
`trussc_app()` writes a pre-build check script, `_tc_check_hot_reload.cmake`, into the build dir. It runs on every build and fails the build when the `TC_HOT_RELOAD` scan result changed since configure (hot reload splits an app into a host exe and a guest shared library, so a change needs a reconfigure). The reusable `release.yml` Windows job always passes such a path (`D:\a\<repo>\<repo>/TrussC/core`). Every app target depends on the check, so `cmake --build` fails whether or not the app uses hot reload. A relative `TRUSSC_DIR` fails too, because `-P` resolves the include against the build dir.
2. **Relative explicit `SOURCES` are never found by the check.** The shared rule skips files that fail `EXISTS`, and `EXISTS` resolves a relative path against the process working directory. The check always says OFF. Configure says ON or OFF depending on where cmake was started, so the configure/build split #234 was meant to remove is back for this layout. Before #248 this layout worked.

title: Known issue #315: Multi-window: close() or setApp() called from the window's own App (update/draw/keyPressed) crashes
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #315, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #315: Multi-window: close() or setApp() called from the window's own App (update/draw/keyPressed) crashes

## Summary
Since #224, an App attached to a secondary window can get that window with `getWindow()`, and the `Window` header tells users to control the window through it "from inside the App". Two calls through that handle crash the whole process when the App makes them from its own `update()`, `draw()` or key handler:

- `getWindow()->close()`: a window that closes itself after a timeout or on a key. `close()` tears down the native window and the App on the spot. The window's tick is still running, and so is sokol's tick wrapper, and both go on using what was just freed.
- `getWindow()->setApp(make_shared<NextScene>())`: scene switching by swapping the window's App. If the Window was the App's only owner, the running App is destroyed inside its own `update()` / `draw()`.

The root cause is older than #224: `close()` and `setApp()` were never safe to call from inside the window's own callbacks. #224 turns this into a one-liner and documents the handle for use from inside the App. Nothing guards against the call and no doc warns about it.

The fix changes when `close()` and `setApp()` take effect, which users can see, so the semantics need an owner decision (see "Suggested fix").

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #310: iOS: default deployment target 15.0 is below what floating-point std::format needs (16.3)

## Summary
The iOS deployment target that trusscli writes into generated projects is 15.0, but floating-point `std::format` (which uses `std::to_chars` for `float` / `double`) is only available on iOS 16.3 and later. Any iOS build of code that formats a float, such as `format("Position: {:.1f} sec", t)`, fails to compile. Many examples do this, so they don't build for iOS with the default settings. CI builds only `AllFeaturesExample` for iOS, so this went unnoticed.

# Known issue #295: Touch-as-mouse uses touches[0] instead of the changed touch: extra mousePressed/mouseReleased with multiple fingers

## Summary
With `touchAsMouse` on (the default), every touch event is converted to a mouse event using `touches[0]`, whichever finger actually changed. sokol puts all active touches into every touch event and flags the changed ones with `changed`. So when a second finger touches down or lifts, TrussC emits another `mousePressed` / `mouseReleased` at the first finger's position, and `mouseDragged` is emitted even when no press is active. On a touch kiosk where several people touch at once, buttons that act on release fire twice. This affects iOS, Android and Web; Windows and macOS have no touch path.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #292: Windows: callAfterAsync/callEveryAsync jitter by up to ~15.6 ms because the timer resolution is never raised
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #292, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #292: Windows: callAfterAsync/callEveryAsync jitter by up to ~15.6 ms because the timer resolution is never raised

## Summary
`Node::callAfterAsync` / `callEveryAsync` are documented as precise, frame-independent timers, "ideal for sequencer clocks and LED/MIDI output timing". On Windows, the scheduler thread waits with `condition_variable::wait_until`, and nothing in TrussC raises the system timer resolution. Each wait can therefore overshoot by up to one default timer tick (about 15.6 ms), so on Windows these timers jitter about as much as the frame-driven `callAfter` / `callEvery`. macOS and Linux are not affected.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #291: tcxHap audio: per-frame PCM sample tables, misparsed lpcm v2 / stsz=1 PCM, and A/V drift on long loops
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #291, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #291: tcxHap audio: per-frame PCM sample tables, misparsed lpcm v2 / stsz=1 PCM, and A/V drift on long loops

## Summary
Three problems in how `HapPlayer` handles the audio track. PCM audio is expanded into one table entry, and one seek + read, per audio frame, which for long files costs hundreds of MB to several GB and a long blocking `load()`. SoundDescription v1/v2 and `lpcm` audio are read with the v0 layout, so, for example, 96 kHz PCM loads as "3 ch, 1 Hz". And video and audio run on separate clocks that are never re-synchronised, so they drift apart over long loops. All three are derived from code; none has been checked against real files yet.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #284: tcxLua: Lua errors escape as sol::error and terminate the app; callAfterAsync/callEveryAsync run Lua on the scheduler thread
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #284, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #284: tcxLua: Lua errors escape as sol::error and terminate the app; callAfterAsync/callEveryAsync run Lua on the scheduler thread

## Summary
A Lua script can take down the host app through tcxLua in two ways:

1. Lua errors (syntax or runtime) are thrown as `sol::error` C++ exceptions out of the calls the examples make from `update()` / `draw()` / `keyPressed()`. Nothing catches them, so the app ends in `std::terminate`. In the bundled `exampleFileReload`, pressing Shift or an arrow key is enough, because `sketch.lua` calls `string.char(key)` and TrussC passes key codes above 255.
2. The generated bindings expose `Node:callAfterAsync` / `callEveryAsync` to Lua. Their callbacks run on the AsyncScheduler thread, so the same `lua_State` is entered from two threads at once. There is no correct way to use them from Lua.

Both come down to one policy: code running inside Lua should not be able to crash the host.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #282: VideoPlayer: setLoop/setVolume/setPan set before load() (or before a reload) never reach the backend

## Summary
`VideoPlayerBase` stores loop, volume, speed and pan, but forwards them to the platform backend only when the player is already loaded. `load()` creates a fresh backend and never re-applies the stored values. So `setLoop(true)` before `load()` does not loop, and a second `load()` on the same player resets the volume to 1.0 while `getVolume()` still returns the old value. This affects macOS, Windows, Linux, Web and tcxHap's `HapPlayer`.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #278: tcxMidi: port removal is not detected; isOpen() stays true and sends are silently dropped

# Known issue #278: tcxMidi: port removal is not detected; isOpen() stays true and sends are silently dropped

## Summary
When a USB-MIDI device is unplugged or a virtual source port goes away, `MidiIn` and `MidiOut` keep reporting `isOpen() == true`. Input stops and output is dropped without any error or log. libremidi offers both port-removal callbacks and an error callback, but tcxMidi subscribes to neither, so an app cannot notice the loss and re-open the port.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #277: VideoGrabber: capture thread keeps pointing at the moved-from mutex_ / pixelsDirty_ after a move

## Summary
`VideoGrabber` is documented as move-only, but moving a grabber after `setup()` leaves the platform capture code holding raw pointers to the moved-from object's `mutex_` and `pixelsDirty_`. The moved-to grabber never sees a new frame, and once the moved-from object is destroyed, the capture thread locks a freed mutex and writes to a freed atomic. Keeping several cameras in a `vector<VideoGrabber>` triggers this when the vector reallocates.

# Known issue #276: VideoGrabber: unplug is never reported, Windows shows black frames for unsupported sizes, and Windows uniqueId is an index

## Summary
Three device-handling gaps in `VideoGrabber`, mostly in the Windows (Media Foundation) backend. An unplugged camera is not reported on any desktop platform: `isInitialized()` stays `true` and the image freezes. On Windows, when the camera has no native mode at the requested size, `setup()` can return `true` while every frame is dropped, which leaves a black image. Also on Windows, `VideoDeviceInfo::uniqueId` is the enumeration index rather than the stable ID the docs promise, so two identical cameras cannot be told apart, and there is no API to open a camera by ID.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #275: tcxDepthCamera: grabber thread outlives backend teardown, setup() does not close first, and timeouts roll the frame back

The base class and `PlaybackDepthCamera` are in this repository; the Orbbec and Azure Kinect backends live in tettou771/tcxOrbbec and tettou771/tcxAzureKinect.

# Known issue #274: saveJson / saveTextFile / Pixels::save truncate in place and report success on write errors (no atomic save)

## Summary

For installations that keep calibration or settings in the data folder (tcxQuadWarp, for example), one bad save loses the configuration, and the next start silently falls back to defaults.

# Known issue #273: Font, Sound, Pixels::load, Lut3D and setLogFile resolve relative paths against the CWD instead of the data folder

## Summary
`Image`, `Json`, `Xml` (#129), `VideoPlayer` and the tcFile.h helpers resolve relative paths through `getDataPath()`, i.e. the data folder next to the executable. `Font`, `Sound`, `Pixels::load`, `Environment::loadFromHDR`, `Lut3D` and tcxHap's `HapPlayer` open the path as given, relative to the process working directory, and so does `Logger::setLogFile`. Started from a terminal in `bin/` the difference is easy to miss, but when a macOS `.app` is opened from Finder (CWD `/`), started as a login item, or a Windows exe is started from Task Scheduler with an empty "Start in" (CWD `C:\Windows\System32`), assets are not found and the log file ends up nowhere or in System32. The docs promise data-folder resolution for fonts and recommend a relative log file name.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #272: Model addons (tcxObj, tcxGltf, tcxPly) pass ANSI-code-page paths on Windows; non-ASCII model paths fail to load

## Summary
The model-loading addons turn `fs::path` into narrow strings with `path.string()`, which on Windows is the ANSI code page (ACP), and then hand those bytes to code that expects UTF-8 (tinyobjloader) or mix them with UTF-8 names read from the model file (texture URIs, `mtllib`). One non-ASCII character anywhere in the absolute path is enough: a Japanese user name or an OneDrive `デスクトップ` folder above the exe makes `ObjLoader::load()` return false, and characters outside the ACP make `.string()` throw `std::system_error`. tcxPly additionally assigns `getDataPath()` (an `fs::path` since #173) to a `std::string`, which should not compile with MSVC. Core already has `internal::pathToUtf8` / `utf8ToPath` for exactly this; the addons don't use them.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #271: Custom Shader draws: the stream-buffer overflow check never fires; over 65536 vertices/indices per frame silently corrupts drawing in Release

## Summary
Each custom `Shader` streams its vertices and indices into fixed buffers of 65536 elements. `executeDeferredShaderDraw()` tries to detect overflow by checking `sg_append_buffer()` for a negative return value, but sokol never returns a negative value. When a frame's shader draws exceed the capacity, Release builds log nothing and issue draws over indices/vertices that were never written. Debug builds abort in sokol validation.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #270: macOS: Fbo::readPixels/copyTo/save call sg_commit() mid-frame and drop the 2D drawn to the screen so far

## Summary
On macOS, `Fbo::readPixels()`, `readPixelsFloat()`, `copyTo()` and `save()` call `sg_commit()` before reading back. Called from `draw()`, this ends sokol's frame in the middle of the app's frame. sokol_gl rewinds, so all 2D drawn to the screen before the call disappears from that frame. If the swapchain pass is open at that point, Debug builds assert. Windows and Linux do not commit here, so the same code behaves differently per platform.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #269: setMaterial()/setEnvironment() keep raw pointers after the Material/Environment is destroyed (use-after-free on the next lit draw)

## Summary
`setMaterial()` and `setEnvironment()` store raw pointers in the current `WindowContext`, and only `clearMaterial()` / `clearEnvironment()` clear them. If the object is destroyed first (a local `Material`, or an `Environment` owned by a Node or scene that gets destroyed), the next lit mesh draw reads freed memory. `Light` had the same problem and was fixed in #200; `Material` and `Environment` were not covered.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #268: PBR/point/Shader pipelines ignore the secondary window's swapchain format, and the PBR pipeline is always indexed

## Summary
The GPU mesh pipelines are chosen from a fixed set of properties that doesn't always match what is being drawn. (1) Outside an FBO, the PBR, point and custom `Shader` pipelines are always built for the main window's swapchain, so drawing into a secondary window uses the wrong color format and sample count. (2) The PBR and shadow pipelines are always indexed, but meshes without indices (valid in glTF, common in hand-built meshes) are sent to them. In Debug builds both hit sokol validation and abort. In the default RelWithDebInfo build validation is off, and the result depends on the backend.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #267: Mesh: GPU buffers are only re-uploaded when the vertex/index count changes, so same-size rebuilds freeze Points and PBR drawing

## Summary
A `Mesh` drawn through a GPU-resident path (Points mode, or PBR when a Material is set and the mesh has normals) only re-uploads its GPU buffers when the vertex or index count changes. None of the mutators mark the buffers dirty. The common openFrameworks pattern of calling `clear()` and re-adding the same number of vertices every frame therefore keeps drawing the first frame's data. Transforms such as `rotateY()` and color changes are ignored the same way.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #266: Windows: exit() does not run on shutdown, logoff or update restart (WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION unhandled)

## Summary
On Windows, when the session ends (shutdown, logoff, a restart for Windows Update, a scheduled `shutdown /r`), a windowed TrussC app is terminated without `App::exit()`, `cleanup()` or the audio shutdown running. Closing the window normally does run them, and macOS already runs them on logout and shutdown. Whatever an app does on exit (save settings, send a DMX blackout, stop a serial device, flush a log) is skipped.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #264: Node: stale global matrix after reparent, and scale-0 nodes hit-test at the parent's origin

## Summary
This covers two correctness problems in Node's global transform and picking. (1) Moving a node to another parent does not invalidate its cached global matrix. `getGlobalPos()`, `globalToLocal()`, the local mouse position in events and RectNode's clip rectangle keep using the old parent until something in the chain moves. (2) `Mat4::inverted()` returns identity for a singular matrix. A node scaled to 0 (for example at the end of `TweenMod::scaleTo(0)`) therefore keeps catching clicks in a rectangle at its parent's origin. Neither problem crashes, but both produce clicks at the wrong place that are hard to trace.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

text:

# Known issue #263: Windows TLS trust: tcxTls skips bundled CAs when the ROOT store is partial; tcxCurl/tcxGPT fail hard when revocation checks are unreachable

## Summary
On Windows, HTTPS and wss:// connections from TrussC can fail while the same URL opens in a browser on the same machine. There are two separate causes, one per TLS stack.

1. `TlsClient` (tcxTls, used by wss:// and MQTT over TLS) loads the Windows ROOT store. If even one certificate in it parses, it never loads the bundled Mozilla CAs, so a root that Windows has not fetched yet is not trusted.
2. tcxCurl's Schannel build checks revocation in hard-fail mode. When the CRL/OCSP servers cannot be reached, every HTTPS request fails. tcxGPT's own curl handles and tcxOpenStreetMap (through `HttpClient`) are affected as well.

Both come down to a default policy choice, following OS policy versus connecting wherever a browser would, and that choice is worth recording.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #262: WebSocketClient: reconnecting from onClose is a use-after-free, and a stalled handshake stays Connecting forever

## Summary
Two gaps in `WebSocketClient`'s connect/disconnect lifecycle, outside the Open state that #220 covered:

1. Calling `ws.connect(url)` from an `onClose` listener destroys the `TcpClient` / `TlsClient` whose receive thread is running that callback, and the thread then reads freed memory. This is the most direct way to write auto-reconnect.
2. If the peer accepts TCP but never completes the TLS handshake (wss://) or never answers the HTTP upgrade (ws:// and wss://), the client stays in `State::Connecting` forever and fires no event. Reconnect logic driven by events never runs.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

title: Known issue #261: TcpClient: send() and connectAsync() can block the main thread indefinitely
text:
[Known bug in the current TrussC: GitHub issue #261, still open as of 2026-10-02. Until it is fixed, TrussC behaves as described here. Mention it only when the question touches this behavior.]

# Known issue #261: TcpClient: send() and connectAsync() can block the main thread indefinitely

## Summary
`TcpClient::send()` has no timeout. When the peer stops reading, it blocks forever in threaded mode, and in non-threaded mode it spins at 100% CPU. `connectAsync()` joins the previous connect attempt, so calling it again while a connect to an unreachable host is still in flight blocks the caller until the OS gives up (about 21 s on Windows, about 127 s on Linux). `disconnect()` and the destructor wait in the same way. `TcpServer` got a non-blocking `sendAsync()` and an idle send timeout in #214, #215 and #218. The client side was left as a follow-up, and no issue tracks it.

(No workaround is written in the issue yet.)

# Known issue #258: D3D11: device removal (TDR, driver update) is never detected; the app keeps running with a black or frozen window

After a TDR (GPU timeout recovery), a driver update or a driver reset, `IDXGISwapChain::Present` fails on every frame, but its result is only used for frame pacing. The app keeps running `update()`/`draw()`, logs nothing, and the window stays black or frozen. Anything that only watches whether the process is alive sees a healthy app.

title: TrussSketch Lua gotchas
text:
# TrussSketch Lua gotchas (read me first)

TrussSketch runs Lua 5.4, not C++. The API NAMES are the same as TrussC C++, but the syntax differs. Watch these:

- Everything is a GLOBAL — no namespace prefix, ever: write `drawCircle(300, 300, 40)`, `Fbo()`, `colors.red`, `TAU`. NEVER write `tc.drawCircle`, `tc::`, or `trussc.` (those are C++ namespaces that do not exist in Lua).
- Call METHODS with a colon: `fbo:begin()`, `mesh:draw()`, `v:length()`. Access FIELDS, static functions, enum values and constants with a dot: `v.x`, `Vec2.fromAngle(a)`, `BlendMode.Add`, `colors.red`, `TAU`.
- Trailing optional arguments really are optional (defaults apply): `setColor(1, 0, 0)` (alpha defaults to 1), `fbo:allocate(600, 600)`, `clear()`. You never need to pad out argument lists.
- Constructors work BOTH ways: `Vec2(10, 20)` and `Vec2.new(10, 20)` are equivalent — use whichever reads better.
- Reserved-word renames — Lua keyword `end` cannot be a method name, so the begin/end pairs are renamed. NEVER call `:end()`. Use:
    - Fbo:     `fbo:begin()` … `fbo:end_fbo()`
    - Shader:  `shader:begin()` … `shader:end_shader()`
    - Camera:  `cam:begin()` … `cam:end_cam()`
- Matrices: `Mat3` / `Mat4` use accessor methods, not index/operator sugar — read and write elements with `m:at(row, col)` and `m:set(...)`.
- Tweens are per-type globals: `TweenFloat`, `TweenVec2`, `TweenVec3`, `TweenColor`. There is NO plain `Tween` — pick the one matching the value you animate.
- Filesystem paths are plain Lua strings (e.g. `"data/img.png"`) — there is no path object.
- NOT bound in Lua (do not use in a sketch): `Thread`, `SoundSource`, `Environment`, `VideoPlayerBase`, `Event<T>`, `ThreadChannel<T>`. These are native-only.
- Cooperative tasks: `spawn(fn)` starts a task, `wait(seconds)` pauses the current task, `forever(fn)` loops fn forever (with an implicit `wait(0)` each iteration so it yields). Use these for animation/sequencing instead of blocking loops.
- Sketch lifecycle functions are OPTIONAL global functions: `function setup() end`, `function update() end`, `function draw() end`. If you don't define one, the host provides a no-op — define only what you need.
- Same core conventions as C++: colors are 0.0–1.0 floats (not 0–255); angles are in radians — use `TAU` (a full turn) instead of PI.

Lua syntax reminders: blocks close with `end`; comments start with `--`; no `#include`, no `::`, no type declarations, no semicolons.

title: enableDepthTest
text:
# enableDepthTest   (Lua function · Graphics - Style)
Re-enable depth test/write on the blend pipelines (compare LESS_EQUAL + depth write, same as the 3D pipeline). Use to restore depth after setBlendMode() mid-scene; persists like the blend mode (across frames and Fbo passes) until disableDepthTest()
ブレンドパイプラインのデプステスト/書き込みを再有効化（LESS_EQUAL比較+デプス書き込み、3Dパイプラインと同じ設定）。シーン途中の setBlendMode() 後にデプスを復元するために使う。ブレンドモードと同様にフレームやFboパスをまたいで disableDepthTest() まで持続する
Lua signatures:
  enableDepthTest()
keywords: depth, z-buffer, occlusion, 3d, blend, restore
rerankText:
enableDepthTest
Re-enable depth test/write on the blend pipelines (compare LESS_EQUAL + depth write, same as the 3D pipeline). Use to restore depth after setBlendMode() mid-scene; persists like the blend mode (across frames and Fbo passes) until disableDepthTest()
Lua signatures:
enableDepthTest()

title: disableDepthTest
text:

Lua signatures:
  disableDepthTest()
keywords: depth, z-buffer, occlusion, overlay, hud, 2d
rerankText:
disableDepthTest

title: App
text:
# App   (Lua type)
Base application class: subclass it and override setup/update/draw and the input callbacks (mousePressed, keyPressed, etc.) to build a TrussC app
アプリケーションの基底クラス。サブクラス化して setup/update/draw や入力コールバック（mousePressed, keyPressed など）をオーバーライドして TrussC アプリを作る
Construct with App(...) or App.new(...):
  App()
Methods (call with :):
  app:setSize([object Object]) — Set the app's size
  app:requestExit([object Object]) — Request the app to exit
  app:isExitRequested([object Object]) — Whether an exit has been requested
  app:keyPressed([object Object]) | app:keyPressed([object Object]) — Key pressed. Use KEY_* constants for special keys, or uppercase char literals for printable keys (e.g. key == 'A', key == '1')
  app:keyReleased([object Object]) | app:keyReleased([object Object]) — Key released
  app:mousePressed([object Object]) | app:mousePressed([object Object]) — Mouse button pressed
  app:mouseReleased([object Object]) | app:mouseReleased([object Object]) — Mouse button released
  app:mouseMoved([object Object]) | app:mouseMoved([object Object]) — Mouse moved
  app:mouseDragged([object Object]) | app:mouseDragged([object Object]) — Mouse dragged
  app:mouseScrolled([object Object]) | app:mouseScrolled([object Object]) — Mouse wheel / trackpad scrolled
  app:touchPressed([object Object]) — Touch began (Android/iOS, multi-touch)
  app:touchMoved([object Object]) — Touch moved (Android/iOS, multi-touch)
  app:touchReleased([object Object]) — Touch ended or was cancelled (check touch.cancelled)
  app:windowResized([object Object]) — Window resized

title: AudioEngine
text:
# AudioEngine   (Lua type)
Singleton miniaudio-based mixer engine. Owns the output device, mixes all playing Sound voices, exposes real-time audioOut / audioIn / audioDeviceChanged events, and an FFT analysis ring buffer. Access via AudioEngine::getInstance(); most apps drive it indirectly through the Sound class and the global initAudio() / shutdownAudio() helpers.

Methods (call with :):
  audioEngine:init() | audioEngine:init(settings) -> boolean — Initialize the engine with defaults, or with an AudioSettings override. Re-init on a running engine migrates active voices to the new settings. Returns true on success.
  audioEngine:shutdown() — Stop and close the audio device.
  audioEngine:getAnalysisBuffer(outBuffer, numSamples) -> number — Copy the latest mixed output samples (mono, L+R average) into outBuffer. numSamples is capped at 4096. Returns the number of samples written. (Global wrapper: getAudioAnalysisBuffer.)
  audioEngine:play(source) | audioEngine:play(buffer) -> shared_ptr — Start a new mixer voice for the given source (eager SoundBuffer or streaming SoundStream) and return its live PlayingSound handle. Usually called indirectly via Sound::play().
  audioEngine:mixAudio(buffer, num_frames, num_channels) — Audio output callback: mix all playing sounds into the buffer (internal, called from the audio thread).

title: PlayingSound
text:
# PlayingSound   (Lua type)
A single live mixer voice returned by AudioEngine::play(). Its fields are the real-time playback state the audio thread reads each callback (volume / pan / speed / loop / playing / paused / mixMode / position) plus the channel routing snapshots. Most fields are atomics so the UI thread can mutate them while the audio thread plays; set them directly.
AudioEngine::play() が返す 1 本のライブミキサーボイス。フィールドは audio thread が各コールバックで読む再生状態 (volume / pan / speed / loop / playing / paused / mixMode / 位置) とチャンネルルーティングのスナップショット。大半は atomic なので UI thread から再生中に書き換えられる。直接設定する
Properties (access with .):
  playingSound.buffer (shared_ptr) — The polymorphic sound source (eager SoundBuffer or streaming SoundStream) this voice plays.
  playingSound.volume (atomic) — Playback volume (0.0-1.0). Stored as an atomic; safe to set from the UI thread while playing.
  playingSound.pan (atomic) — Stereo pan (-1.0 left, 0.0 center, 1.0 right). Atomic.
  playingSound.speed (atomic) — Playback speed (0.5 half, 1.0 normal, 2.0 double). Atomic.
  playingSound.loop (atomic) — Loop the voice when it reaches the end. Atomic.
  playingSound.playing (atomic) — True while this voice is active in the mixer. Atomic.
  playingSound.paused (atomic) — True while paused (still a live voice, but not advancing). Atomic.
  playingSound.mixMode (atomic) — Channel mix policy when no explicit channelMap is set (Auto / DownmixMono). Stored as an atomic int holding the MixMode value.
  playingSound.positionF (number) — Floating-point playback cursor in source samples; advances by speed * rateRatio each output frame.
  playingSound.rateRatio (number) — Source-to-engine sample-rate ratio (buffer sampleRate / engine sampleRate), set when queued so the voice plays at correct pitch regardless of engine rate.
Related: AudioEngine, SoundSource, MixMode

  window:setApp([object Object]) — Attach an App to this window — the only way to give a window content. The App's full lifecycle (setup/update/draw/key/mouse/windowResized + RectNode size sync) runs against this window. One App per window
  window:getApp([object Object]) — Get the App attached to this window

  window:getTitle([object Object]) — Last title set for this window (via WindowSettings or setTitle)

# Xml   (Lua type)
XML document wrapper around pugixml. Loads, saves and queries XML; node-level access is via XmlNode returned from root() and child().

Construct with Xml(...) or Xml.new(...):

Methods (call with :):
  xml:load(path) -> boolean — Load an XML document from a file. Relative paths are resolved via getDataPath. Returns true on success.
  xml:parse(str) -> boolean — Parse an XML document from a string. Returns true on success.
  xml:save(path, indent = "  ") -> boolean — Save the document to a file. Relative paths are resolved via getDataPath. indent sets the per-level indentation string. Returns true on success.
  xml:toString(indent = "  ") -> string — Serialize the document to an XML string. indent sets the per-level indentation string.
  xml:root() | xml:root() -> XmlNode — Get the document's root element node.
  xml:addRoot(name) -> XmlNode — Append a new root element with the given name and return it.
  xml:child(name) -> XmlNode — Find a direct child node of the document by name.
  xml:document() | xml:document() -> XmlDocument — Access the underlying pugixml document for advanced operations.
  xml:empty() -> boolean — Return true if the document has no content.
  xml:addDeclaration(version = "1.0", encoding = "UTF-8") — Prepend an XML declaration (<?xml ...?>) with the given version and encoding.

title: Tasks (spawn/wait/forever)
text:
# Tasks: spawn / wait / forever   (Lua — TrussSketch cooperative tasks)
TrussSketch runs cooperative tasks (coroutines) so you can animate or sequence things over time without blocking draw().

  spawn(fn) — Start a cooperative task; runs until fn returns.
      協調タスクを開始。fnが終わるまで動く
  wait(seconds) — Pause the current task for the given number of seconds.
      現在のタスクを指定秒だけ一時停止する
  forever(fn) — Repeat fn every frame, with an implicit wait(0) between iterations.
      毎フレームfnを繰り返す（暗黙のwait(0)付き）

Inside a task, wait(sec) pauses just that task. forever(fn) repeats fn forever, with an implicit wait(0) each loop so it yields.
keywords: spawn, wait, forever, task, coroutine, async, animation, sequence, タスク, 待つ, 繰り返し

title: TrussSketch constants
text:
# TrussSketch constants   (Lua)
Global constants available in every sketch (use the bare name):

  Baseline — Direction shorthand for Direction::Baseline (text baseline)
  Bottom — Direction shorthand for Direction::Bottom

  HALF_TAU — Half circle (PI)

  KEY_DOWN — Down arrow key
  KEY_ENTER — Enter/Return key
